Nodes weigh identities pairwise. Each epoch they measure how much one member's work reveals about another's, task held fixed: two keys whose work is mutually predictable - same phrasing, blind spots, shortcut - are booked as one entry.

A cedar grove holds because each tree draws on its own soil; a lantern passed along a line of clones lights one ledge only.

The attacker pays: to count separately, a key must say something unpredictable from every other key its owner holds. Independence cannot be rented, only earned through separate data and errors. A thousand aliases fold into one unit.
